CharacterCreator.Heading: How would you like to create this character?
CharacterCreator.Description: You can fill in the sheet freely or use the Character Creator, which will guide each creation step according to the Symbaroum rules.
CharacterCreator.DecisionHint: Closing this window without choosing will show the question again; select the option below to dismiss it for this character.
CharacterCreator.DoNotShowAgain: Do not show again for this character

Guide.Title: How to create a character
Guide.StepOneText: Start by choosing an archetype and one of its suggested occupations. Archetypes and occupations are starting points: they bring the character to life and provide a quick way into the game, but do not restrict choices in later steps.
Guide.StepTwoText: The eight Attributes form the backbone of the character. Choose a typical distribution to use each value once or use point buy to build the combination you want.
Guide.StepThreeText: Race describes the character's origin and nature. It grants mandatory traits or a cultural choice; some special traits may also be selected, but use one Ability choice in the next step.
Guide.StepFourText: Abilities represent the character's training and special talents. Purchase them freely with Experience or use one of the starting distributions. Optional racial traits already chosen also count toward the cost or occupy Novice slots.
Guide.StepFiveText: The Shadow reveals the character's spiritual essence. Choose colors, textures, and signs that express a bond with civilization, nature, or darkness.
Guide.StepSixText: Martial Abilities determine part of the starting equipment. Items granted by them, money, and camping equipment are added automatically; if none grants a weapon, choose a starting combination.
Guide.StepSevenText: Bring the numbers to life: define who the character is, where they came from, how they present themselves, what they seek, and how their spiritual essence manifests as a Shadow. If they have the Contacts trait, their network is also defined in this step.
Guide.StepEightText: Record the other characters, the group's name, and the goal everyone shares. The collective goal gives the Game Master a starting point for missions, encounters, and adventures.

Hunter.Name: Hunter
Hunter.Summary: Hunters track prey with ranged weapons, traps, poisons, and hunting techniques.

Warrior.Name: Warrior
Warrior.Summary: Warriors face danger head-on as combatants, leaders, guardians, and weapon specialists.

Mystic.Name: Mystic
Mystic.Summary: Mystics control the world through traditions, powers, rituals, faith, or pacts—always under the risk of Corruption.

Rogue.Name: Rogue
Rogue.Summary: Rogues survive through cunning and versatility, seizing opportunities and reacting quickly to danger.

Occupation.Title: Character Creator — Choose Your Occupation
Occupation.ArchetypeSelectionText: The archetype describes the character's broad path and groups occupations with similar talents and styles. It guides creation but does not restrict later choices.
Occupation.ArchetypeRuleText: Under the Advanced Player's Guide rules, a character must possess at least three Abilities related to an archetype before acquiring its Archetypal Ability; Novice rank is sufficient.
Occupation.ProfessionNotice: Professions are advancement options, not initial creation choices.
Occupation.SelectionHint: Your occupation guides your concept but does not restrict the character's future choices.
Occupation.CustomNameRequired: Enter a name for the custom occupation.
Occupation.CustomQuotePlaceholder: A phrase that represents the character
Occupation.CustomSummaryPlaceholder: Describe the training, role, and style of this occupation.
Occupation.CustomHint: Create your own concept using the book occupations as inspiration. The occupation does not restrict choices in later steps.

Attributes.Title: Character Creator — Distribute Attributes
Attributes.Heading: The Attributes
Attributes.Introduction: Whenever an action has dramatic importance, the character makes a Success Test. The higher the relevant Attribute, the greater the chance of success.
Attributes.TypicalRules: Distribute the values 5, 7, 9, 10, 10, 11, 13, and 15 among the eight Attributes. Only one value may be 15; none may be higher than 15 or lower than 5.
Attributes.TypicalHint: Choose one value for each Attribute. Assigned numbers are crossed out and disappear from the other options.
Attributes.PointBuyRules: Distribute exactly 80 points among the eight Attributes. Each value must remain between 5 and 15, and only one Attribute may reach 15.
Attributes.PointBuyHint: Lower an Attribute to release points, then use + to invest them elsewhere. The distribution is complete only when the counter returns to zero.
Attributes.SpendAll: Points still need to be distributed
Attributes.Invalid: The distribution does not meet the Attribute creation rules.

accurate.Name: Accurate
accurate.Description: Represents coordination, precision, and assertiveness. It is used to hit targets with blows, thrown objects, and ranged weapons, usually opposed by Quick.

cunning.Name: Cunning
cunning.Description: Represents wit, knowledge, common sense, and education. It is used to recall facts, solve logical problems, and perform research.

discreet.Name: Discreet
discreet.Description: Represents the ability to act quietly and unseen. It is used to hide, follow someone, smuggle, or steal, and is usually opposed by Vigilant.

persuasive.Name: Persuasive
persuasive.Description: Represents the ability to influence others through words, voice, appearance, and body language, usually opposed by Resolute.

quick.Name: Quick
quick.Description: Represents reflexes, balance, agility, and speed. It determines initiative and helps with jumps, dodges, and acrobatic maneuvers.

resolute.Name: Resolute
resolute.Description: Represents resistance to social pressure, mental control, and Corruption, and is tied to the use of mystical powers. A low value is risky.

strong.Name: Strong
strong.Description: Represents physical strength, the ability to endure pain, and resistance to poison and disease. It also determines the character's base Toughness.

vigilant.Name: Vigilant
vigilant.Description: Represents alertness, keen senses, and the ability to notice details in the surroundings, often opposed by an enemy's Discreet.

ambrian.Name: Ambrian
ambrian.Summary: Heirs to the realm south of the Titans, Ambrians came to Davokar with organization, ambition and strong social divisions.

history.Paragraph1: According to the scholars of Ordo Magica, the peoples of Ambria and Davokar descend from the same tribe, although neither barbarians nor the Queen's People regard the other as close kin.
history.Paragraph2: Queen Korinthia's claim on Ambria rests on an ancestral bond with the region. The related languages support it, while the theory that both peoples descend from a family tree rooted in ancient Symbaroum remains disputed.
history.Paragraph3: The cultures differ greatly. Ambrians left blighted Alberetor twenty years ago, bringing architecture, learning, economy and social hierarchy. Their disciplined armies excel in open country, while barbarian knowledge prevails in the forest.
history.Paragraph4: Most Ambrians avoid travelling deep into Davokar, except treasure-hunters, religious zealots and settlers hoping to escape the Queen's control.
history.Paragraph5: A united barbarian resistance troubles the court. Haloban's fall in Year 10 and the Templars' failed assault on Karvosti in Year 16 taught the Ambrians to approach Davokar cautiously.

names.Paragraph1: Ambrian female names usually end in -a and male names in -o. Many noble names end in -gai, -goi or -mei; x is uncommon and j is often replaced by i.
names.male: Aro, Beremo, Demeon, Edogai, Gadramei, Iasogoi, Jomilo, Karlio, Malliano, Peonio.
names.female: Abesina, Elindra, Elionara, Levia, Mehira, Ordelia, Revina, Suria, Variol, Vidina.

surnames.Paragraph1: Apart from nobles and their houses, Ambrians do not use family names. Famous people may earn honorific surnames tied to their deeds, such as Lasifor Nightpitch and Lysindra Goldengrasp.

barbarian.Name: Barbarian
barbarian.Summary: The barbarian clans have known Davokar and its borders for generations, living under chieftains and ancient traditions.

history.Paragraph1: Ordo Magica claims that barbarians and Ambrians descend from the same tribe, though neither people welcomes the comparison. Their related languages and Symbaroum's ruins fuel theories of a common origin.
history.Paragraph2: Barbarians have long been governed by chieftains, yet enjoy greater freedom than southern tenants and peasants. Not every leader imposes a rigid way of life.
history.Paragraph3: Witches guide the clans lightly through taboos and broad rules: revere nature, never abuse it and avoid the darkest reaches of the forest.
history.Paragraph4: Clans live independently except during border disputes. Their leaders answer to the High Chieftain at Karvosti, who acts more as arbiter than absolute ruler.
history.Paragraph5: The High Chieftain is expected to unite the clans against invaders. The Templars' defeat at Karvosti in Year 16 showed how dangerous a united barbarian resistance could be.

names.Paragraph1: Female barbarian names tend to end in -a; male names in -mar, -mon or -mer. Double consonants are rare, and a, o and u are especially favored.
names.male: Adelar, Gadramon, Haloban, Konarad, Lothar, Odaban, Rábaiamon, Taran, Tharaban, Vikomer.
names.female: Adela, Aloeta, Eferneya, Elmea, Elda, Galoma, Horosa, Karona, Verama, Yagaba.

changeling.Name: Changeling
changeling.Summary: Left among humans as children, changelings live between two natures and an identity often denied to them.

history.Paragraph1: Elves have stolen human babies and left changelings in their cradles for as long as barbarian witches can remember. Since the Ambrians arrived, cases have appeared in every social caste, with no clear elven purpose.
history.Paragraph2: A changeling looks human in childhood and develops elven features in adolescence without becoming a true elf. It matures at a human pace, then lives for a very long time. Scholars dispute whether changelings are made by elven magic or are elven offspring whose natural cycle was interrupted.
history.Paragraph3: Their lives are difficult. Few remain with their families after their nature is revealed. Witches and mages sometimes take them as assistants; most survive alone, becoming bitter and melancholy or frivolous and indifferent.

names.Paragraph1: Some keep elven names after being abandoned or cast out; others take a new, sometimes extravagant name as an act of defiance and independence.
names.male: Aka, Ardri, Eneáno, Feon, Ganderald, Goriol, Ibliglin, Kalfu, Radomaramei, Sinue.
names.female: Bekora, Danive, Yeloéna, Elorinda, Hinéua, Kinlegelana, Riamata, Roha, Seanua, Varaneia.

goblin.Name: Goblin
goblin.Summary: Goblins live intensely through their few decades and occupy marginalized positions in Ambrian society.

history.Paragraph1: Little is known of goblin origins, but their presence south of Davokar is obvious. The tribe near Thistle Hold became unpopular for its impulsive temperament and strange social games.
history.Paragraph2: Goblin life is short: young at five, adult at ten and old at twenty. Thirty is rare and no forty-year-old is known. Most return voluntarily to Davokar when death approaches.
history.Paragraph3: They are tolerated in Thistle Hold because they perform dirty and dangerous work. Crowds enter at dawn and are driven out again at night.
history.Paragraph4: Some escape this pattern as treasure-hunters, servants to wealthy households or monastery pupils. Garm Wormwriggler became the most famous successful treasure-hunter among them.

names.Paragraph1: Goblin names follow few conventions and may change or gain syllables after major events. In general, a longer name signals higher status in the tribe.
names.male: Alfbolg, Barra, Goltas, Illefons, Ler, Rosti, Shigg, Tengel, Ul.
names.female: Aa, Fosa, Guhula, Hugalea, Tulga, Udelia, Ufa, Wamba, Yla, Yppa.

ogre.Name: Ogre
ogre.Summary: Ogres emerge fully grown and without memories from Davokar, learning from whoever finds them.

history.Paragraph1: Ogres are strange solitary creatures that wander out of Davokar fully grown, without memories or identity. The humans or goblins who find them give them names and teach them about the world.
history.Paragraph2: Ogre stories range from humorous to mystical and horrific. Witches take them as guards, explorers value their strength and goblin gangs use them as heavy-handed enforcers.
history.Paragraph3: In southern Davokar, stories tell of Deterror and Vitrona, a witch-trained scout and his huge ogre friend. Their adventures in Symbaroum's ruins became popular songs in Thistle Hold.

names.Paragraph1: Ogres seem to have no names of their own. Others give them nicknames based on size, appearance or temperament; Ordo Magica suspects the creature considers that sufficient.
names.examples: Bauta, Big Brute, Brawler, Bull, Calm, Heavy, Nervous, Odd, Rage, Strange, Ugly.

elf.Name: Elf
elf.Summary: The elves of the Iron Pact guard Davokar and fight to keep the darkness beneath its roots asleep.

history.Paragraph1: Davokar's elves belong to the Iron Pact, an order charged with preventing the evil sleeping beneath the forest from awakening. Many were born into the order and have never seen the elven lands of the west.
history.Paragraph2: Summer elves form the backbone of the guardians: vigilant hunters armed with spears and bows. War against abominations and taboo-breakers has reduced their numbers and made alliances with humans increasingly important.
history.Paragraph3: Elves are Long-lived and Pariahs among humans. Wisdom of the Ages may be acquired as an Ability. The book recommends a summer elf for a starting character, as older elves are far more powerful and experienced.

names.Paragraph1: Spring and summer elves receive double names; after later dormancies they may shorten or replace them. Their names usually contain more vowels than consonants.
names.male: Alal-Roak, Dorael-Ri, Eloan-Eo, Elori, Godrai, Mearoel, Saran-Ri, TelKeriel, Kil-Ano.
names.female: Ahara-Vei, Eleanea, Leiana, Gaina-Anali, Keri-Las, Mael-Melian, Naelial, Tara-Kel, Teara-Teana.

dwarf.Name: Dwarf
dwarf.Summary: Dwarves are bound to family, the spoken word, and the fate of the world itself, while keeping their origins shrouded in secrets.

history.Paragraph1: Dwarven history is a mystery even to scholars. In Yndaros, their families look toward the future and protect a culture of codes, double meanings, and absolute loyalty to kin.
history.Paragraph2: Dwarven morality distinguishes family from outsiders: the elders' will outweighs the individual's, and actions against outsiders are judged chiefly by how they affect the family.
history.Paragraph3: Every dwarf has Natural Heritage, Absolute Memory, and Pariah. Retribution may be acquired as an Ability; for dwarves alone, that power causes no Corruption when learned or used.

names.Paragraph1: Dwarven names favor hard consonants and do not vary by gender. Younger dwarves must earn the right to use the family surname.
names.examples: Artek, Bolkor, Brana, Dobril, Dranek, Dusa, Jarok, Lazek, Margor, Mirek, Radmil, Stana, Vesnek, Vlador, Yaruk.

abductedHuman.Name: Abducted Human
abductedHuman.Summary: Raised among elves after being taken as a child, the abductee knows the forest and lives between two peoples.

history.Paragraph1: Elves abduct human children for reasons that changed over time: first to understand humanity, later to create mediators, and more recently to reinforce the Iron Pact's ranks.
history.Paragraph2: Abductees are loyal students and many hunt beside summer elves. Even so, few elves regard them as equals, however much courage and wisdom they display.
history.Paragraph3: Abducted humans have Bushcraft and speak Elvish. They can only write the language after acquiring Loremaster.

names.Paragraph1: Their foster parents choose short names that are easy to pronounce and remember, usually attempting to imitate human naming sounds.
names.examples: Use a simple human name or a short name chosen by the character's elven foster parents.

troll.Name: Troll
troll.Summary: Trolls belong to a subterranean civilization of artisans, warriors, and singers shaped by challenges and collective strength.

history.Paragraph1: Trolls, goblins, and ogres share an origin. Some goblins entering a chrysalis in the depths survive and awaken as trolls; failures in that process may produce the beings called ogres.
history.Paragraph2: Troll society measures each person by what they contribute to the community. Physical, artistic, and mystical contests are part of social life, and even ritualized disputes can end in death.
history.Paragraph3: Trolls are Long-lived and Pariahs. Armored, Natural Weapon, Regeneration, and Robust may be acquired as Abilities; choose only what the character can pay for with starting Experience.

names.Paragraph1: Names do not vary by gender and may change many times. The letter X is common among older or more powerful trolls.
names.examples: Young: Aka, Aroha, Erula, Hibne, Ogmaka, Raham, Riomata, Skadal, Verhar. Old or powerful: Aravarx, Etaxa, Noxar, Ognyx, Rirbax, Vouax, Uhux.

undead.Name: Undead
undead.Summary: A dead person whose mind and will remain, forced to hide their nature and sustain a body that no longer lives.

history.Paragraph1: A new kind of undead has appeared in Ambria: people who should have died rise with their minds intact while their cold bodies slowly decay toward final death.
history.Paragraph2: Undead do not sleep, breathe, or eat normally. They recover Toughness by consuming fresh flesh or blood and must hide their condition from witchhunters, Black Cloaks, and angry mobs.
history.Paragraph3: The character begins fully corrupted and with Undead I. Grave Cold and Terrify may be acquired as optional Abilities. This race changes central rules for healing, Corruption, and social interaction.

names.Paragraph1: Undead normally retain the name they had in life but may adopt a false identity to conceal their death.
names.examples: Use the character's living name or the identity they built after returning.

contacts.Name: Contacts
contacts.Description: The character has a network of acquaintances tied to a region or social group.

privileged.Name: Privileged
privileged.Description: The character belongs to the social elite and may use status, resources and influence.

bushcraft.Name: Bushcraft
bushcraft.Description: The character knows how to find food, shelter and safe paths in the wild.

longLived.Name: Long-lived
longLived.Description: The race matures slowly and may live for many centuries.

shortLived.Name: Short-lived
shortLived.Description: The race grows quickly and rarely lives more than a few decades.

pariah.Name: Pariah
pariah.Description: The character belongs to a people treated with suspicion and hostility by dominant society.

shapeshifter.Name: Shapeshifter
shapeshifter.Description: Allows changing appearance and, with greater mastery, assuming more radical forms.

survivalInstinct.Name: Survival Instinct
survivalInstinct.Description: A sharp racial instinct helps the character avoid blows and survive threats.

robust.Name: Robust
robust.Description: The character has size, strength and physical endurance far beyond the ordinary.

wisdomOfAges.Name: Wisdom of the Ages
wisdomOfAges.Description: The elves' collective memory grants temporary access to the knowledge of earlier generations at the cost of temporary Corruption.

naturalHeritage.Name: Natural Heritage
naturalHeritage.Description: The creature is bound to the substance of the world, has no soul, and suffers physical damage instead of Corruption.

absoluteMemory.Name: Absolute Memory
absoluteMemory.Description: The character has trained their memory to preserve information with extraordinary precision.

retribution.Name: Retribution
retribution.Description: A power tied to dwarven speech and heritage. For a dwarf, Retribution causes no Corruption when acquired or used.

armored.Name: Armored
armored.Description: The creature's skin or natural shell protects it like armor.

naturalWeapon.Name: Natural Weapon
naturalWeapon.Description: Claws, fangs, horns, or another body part function as a natural weapon.

regeneration.Name: Regeneration
regeneration.Description: The body recovers wounds supernaturally, though certain sources of damage may prevent the effect.

undead.Name: Undead
undead.Description: The character does not breathe, sleep, or heal normally and must consume fresh flesh or blood to recover Toughness.

tombCold.Name: Grave Cold
tombCold.Description: The chill presence of death affects those who draw near the undead.

terrify.Name: Terrify
terrify.Description: The creature reveals its monstrous nature to spread fear among its enemies.

Contacts.Title: Character Creator — Who Are Your Contacts?
Contacts.Required: Enter the main network and explain how the character relates to it.
Contacts.Heading: Who Are Your Contacts?
Contacts.StepText: You chose the Contacts trait. Define the region, organization, or social group the network belongs to and some important people within it.
Contacts.Introduction: Contacts represents a network of acquaintances connected to a region or social group. It may be an entire organization — such as the Sun Church, Ordo Magica, a clan, a guild, or the army — and need not be limited to one NPC.

InPlay.Declare: Tell the Game Master which contact in the network the character seeks and what they need.
InPlay.Connect: Explain why that person or organization would know the character and might help.
InPlay.Master: The Game Master decides who is available, what they know, how long the help takes, and which conditions or tests fit the scene.

CanProvide.Information: rumors, specialized information, local news, and clues;
CanProvide.Introduction: introductions, social access, and referrals to capable people;
CanProvide.Help: reasonable favors, shelter, messages, or practical help appropriate to the group.

Contacts.Limits: Contacts is not absolute control over NPCs or an unlimited source of money, soldiers, or equipment. Favors may require time, discretion, reciprocity, or place the character in debt.
Contacts.QuickHint: Choose the network and explain your connection to it. All other details are optional.
Contacts.NetworkPlaceholder: E.g. Sun Church in Yndaros, Ordo Magica, clan Baiaga, Thieves' Guild...
Contacts.NetworkHint: This is the trait's main scope. Make it specific enough to create stories, yet broad enough to include more than one person.
Contacts.Relationship: How does the character know this network?
Contacts.RelationshipPlaceholder: Describe how the connection began, why they still trust the character, and how help is usually requested...
Contacts.PeopleHint: Optional. Record existing NPCs or invent some now. They are not automatically created as Actors; the names are references for the player and Game Master.
Contacts.Access: What help or information is usually available?
Contacts.AccessPlaceholder: E.g. political rumors, artifact identification, safe passage, discreet shelter...
Contacts.Complications: What does the network expect in return?
Contacts.ComplicationsPlaceholder: E.g. future favors, secrecy, fair payment, protecting a member...

Abilities.NotEnoughExperience: There is not enough XP to purchase this Ability at this level.
Abilities.MysticalPowerChoiceIntro: Each power counts as one Ability. Choose the power and rank to learn; you may purchase more than one power.
Abilities.NoMysticalPowers: No accessible Mystical Power is available in the world.
Abilities.NoFilteredMysticalPowers: No Mystical Powers belong to the selected source books.
Abilities.RitualChoiceIntro: Ritualist grants 1 ritual at Novice, 3 at Adept and 6 at Master. The selected rituals will be added to the sheet.
Abilities.NoRituals: No accessible Ritual is available in the world.
Abilities.NoFilteredRituals: No Rituals belong to the selected source books.
Abilities.RitualCapacityFull: Every Ritual slot at this rank is already filled.
Abilities.InvalidSpecialChoice: Choose every required Mystical Power or Ritual before continuing.
Abilities.AdvancedRuleInvalid: An archetypal or profession Ability does not meet the Advanced Player's Guide requirements.
Abilities.ArchetypeRequirement: This Ability requires at least {count} other Abilities from the archetype's list.
Abilities.ProfessionAbility: Available only to members of the {profession} profession. Professions are progression goals, not starting occupations.
Abilities.ProfessionAbilityLocked: Profession-exclusive Ability; unavailable during initial creation.
Abilities.ProfessionChoiceLocked: Profession-exclusive Power or Ritual; unavailable during initial creation.

Professions.Title: Advanced Guide Professions
Professions.Rules: Professions are progression goals. To enter one, the character must meet every requirement and have at least one required Ability at Master rank. Exclusive capabilities remain visible for reference but cannot be purchased during initial creation.

AdvancedTraits.Title: Boons and Burdens
AdvancedTraits.Rules: Optional Advanced Player's Guide rule: each Boon costs 5 XP and each Burden grants 5 additional XP during creation.
AdvancedTraits.Limits: Book recommendation: no more than 2 or 3 Boons and 1 or 2 Burdens. The creator limits selections to 3 Boons and 2 Burdens. Click a name to open its original sheet.

Traditions.PurchaseExplanation: To belong to this tradition, the character must purchase the {ability} Ability. This choice represents their training, principles, and way of handling Corruption.
Traditions.ProfessionPurchaseExplanation: {ability} is a Profession-exclusive Ability. Under the Advanced Player's Guide rules, a profession is a progression goal: the character must meet its required Abilities and have at least one of them at Master level.

witchcraft.Name: Witchcraft
witchcraft.Introduction: The oldest mystical tradition is rooted in the wilds of Davokar. Its practitioners read the world through winds, blood, and all growing things.
witchcraft.Doctrine: Witchcraft follows three dangerous paths: the white path of winds and spirits, the red path marked by blood, and the green path covered in roots and vegetation. Witches regard them as parts of one natural balance.
witchcraft.Titles: Each barbarian village commonly shelters a witch and an apprentice. A clan's witches form a coven led by a Keeper; at Karvosti, the Huldra advises the High Chieftain and holds the tradition's most respected position.
witchcraft.Powers: Bend Will, Curse, Entangling Vines, Inherit Wound, Larvae Boil, Lay on Hands, Maltransformation, Nature's Embrace, Shapeshift, Storm Arrow, and Witch Hammer.
witchcraft.Rituals: Borrow Beast, Familiar, Nature's Lullaby, Necromancy, Oracle, Quick Growth, Turn Weather, Witch Circle, and Blood Bond.
witchcraft.Corruption: Corruption is understood as nature's answer to what the witch demands of the world. Every use of power must be weighed against necessity, and some witches accept sacrifice to protect their people.

sorcery.Name: Sorcery
sorcery.Introduction: Sorcerers seek power in tainted sources and study forces other traditions fear to touch. Their path offers swift results but exacts a price from body and soul.
sorcery.Doctrine: Sorcery gathers powers and rituals fueled by taint. Its practitioners learn to recognize, withstand, and exploit Corruption without surrendering completely to it.
sorcery.Titles: No single order governs sorcerers. Many learn in isolation, from secret masters, or through forbidden texts and artifacts; they are therefore hunted and studied by organizations such as the Black Cloaks.
sorcery.Powers: Bend Will, Curse, Larvae Boil, Unholy Aura, and Unnoticeable Strike.
sorcery.Rituals: Enslave, Possess, Desecrating Rite, and Exchange Shadow.
sorcery.Corruption: The sorcerer sees Corruption as an inevitable part of a dying world. The tradition teaches how to walk beside darkness and use its strength while staying far enough away not to be consumed.

wizardry.Name: Wizardry
wizardry.Introduction: Wizardry is the tradition of the Ordo Magica. Its practitioners study nature's fundamental laws and learn to alter them through discipline, reason, and trained will.
wizardry.Doctrine: To wizards, the world is deeply magical and can be understood without depending on the will of gods. The long, demanding education rewards perseverance with systematic command of its mysteries.
wizardry.Titles: Progress begins as Apprentice, continues through Adept and Magistrate, and reaches Master. Each Ordo Magica chapter is governed by a Chapter Master, while the whole order answers to the Grand Master.
wizardry.Powers: Anathema, Bend Will, Brimstone Cascade, Confusion, Illusory Correction, Levitate, Mind-Throw, True Form, Unnoticeable, and Wall of Fire.
wizardry.Rituals: Clairvoyance, False Terrain, Flaming Servant, Illusion, Magic Circle, Necromancy, Seven-league Stride, Soul Stone, Telepathic Interrogation, and Wizard's Sanctum.
wizardry.Corruption: The Ordo Magica describes Corruption as a natural reaction to mystical power. Knowledge, method, and caution let a wizard provoke that reaction without losing control.

theurgy.Name: Theurgy
theurgy.Introduction: Theurgy is the tradition of Prios's mystical priests. Its powers are regarded as the Sun God's light radiating through faithful champions chosen to protect humanity.
theurgy.Doctrine: Theurgs sustain the Church through prayer, devotion, and mystical power. They see themselves as Prios's emissaries and defenders of human order against night, wilderness, and corruption.
theurgy.Titles: Initiates assist and learn from the Church's Brothers and Sisters, who serve senior theurgs known as Fathers or Mothers. Obedience to superiors is a central virtue of the tradition.
theurgy.Powers: Anathema, Blessed Shield, Inherit Wound, Lay on Hands, Levitate, Prios's Burning Glass, Sacred Aura, True Form, Unnoticeable, and Witch Hammer.
theurgy.Rituals: Command Confession, Exorcism, Holy Smoke, Judgment Bonds, Oracle, Patron Saint, Purging Fire, Heretic's Trail, and Sanctifying Rite.
theurgy.Corruption: Theurgs associate Corruption with what grows without cultivation and control. Even so, every devotee must accept the risk of taint and keep their inner flame alive when facing darkness.

trollSinging.Name: Troll Singing
trollSinging.Introduction: As old as the trolls' collective memory, Troll Singing preserves stories, harmonies, and truths about the world before Corruption.
trollSinging.Doctrine: The skalds' songs, the smiths' hammering, and warriors' claws form the great hymn of troll life. Its powers chiefly influence the mind, and several are hymns maintained while the singer performs other actions.
trollSinging.Titles: Troll Singers use no formal titles. A promising singer learns from a master, serves the rulers when ready, and later passes the tradition to a new apprentice.
trollSinging.Powers: Dancing Weapon, Confusion, Battle Hymn, Hymn of Weakening, Heroic Hymn, and Retribution.
trollSinging.Rituals: Restore and Retrieve. The tradition has few rituals of its own, but its skalds may learn rituals from other traditions.
trollSinging.Corruption: Willingly accepting Corruption is unthinkable to most singers. Their songs recall the world before the taint and the trolls' duty to the Iron Pact and Davokar.

staffMagic.Name: Staff Magic
staffMagic.Introduction: Staff Mages are ascetic warrior monks who regard themselves as heirs to the last emperor of Symbaroum's guard and seek to repair the failure that preceded the empire's fall.
staffMagic.Doctrine: The runestaff is an extension of the mage's soul and their principal weapon. The order fights abominations, sorcerers, and reckless use of Corruption while searching for the ancient emperor's rightful heir.
staffMagic.Titles: The order distinguishes the Staffless, apprentices without their own weapon; Runestaffs, members who have received one; and Staff Masters.
staffMagic.Powers: Dancing Weapon, Anathema, Staff Projectile, Sphere, and Protective Runes.
staffMagic.Rituals: Blood Storm and Tremor. Its rituals are woven into and stored in the staff, which cannot receive another power or ritual until activation; rituals from other traditions work normally.
staffMagic.Corruption: The order treats Corruption as a consequence of careless power. It must be avoided because enemies can turn it against the mage and because reckless magic also wounds the surrounding world.

symbolism.Name: Symbolism
symbolism.Introduction: Brought from the east by mystics who settled in Clan Vajvod territory, Symbolism reshapes the world through runes, signs, and patterns charged with power.
symbolism.Doctrine: Symbolists paint, write, and carve symbols. Their protection comes from the time and care invested in creating runes, whether drawn on perishable materials, carved permanently, or written as light in the air.
symbolism.Titles: Apprentices are Followers or Spools; initiated members are Weavers. Master Weaver is honorary, and many members adopt names such as Sign Carver, Painter of Fate, or Artificer of Power.
symbolism.Powers: Draining Glyph, Protective Runes, Banishing Seal, and Blinding Symbol.
symbolism.Rituals: Spell Trap, Distant Writing, Carve Runic Tattoo, and Runic Guardian.
symbolism.Corruption: Symbolists suffer no permanent Corruption when learning the tradition's powers or crafting symbols. Each activated symbol causes only 1 point of temporary Corruption; rituals follow the normal rules.

artifactCrafting.Name: Artifact Crafting
artifactCrafting.Introduction: Artifact crafting is a nearly lost mystical practice preserved chiefly among trolls and recently passed to elves, abducted humans, and scholars of the Ordo Magica.
artifactCrafting.Doctrine: Artifact Crafters combine knowledge, craftsmanship, and mystical power to infuse objects with lasting effects. The practice is a Profession and therefore a progression goal rather than a normal starting option.
artifactCrafting.Titles: A practitioner must master Blacksmith, Loremaster, and Ritualist; Mystical Power is useful but optional. Joining the Profession requires every required Ability and at least one of them at Master level.
artifactCrafting.Powers: At Novice, the character can make Novice lesser artifacts; at Adept, Adept lesser artifacts become available; at Master, the character reaches Master lesser artifacts. The original artifact sheets still define costs, effects, and requirements.
artifactCrafting.Rituals: Each creation requires materials, time, and a Cunning test appropriate to the Ability rank. Available secrets may depend on the character's tradition when the group uses the optional Secrets of the Traditions rule.
artifactCrafting.Corruption: Crafting and binding power into objects remains subject to the Corruption rules stated by the Ability and individual artifacts. The crafter should consult the original sheet before beginning the process.

Shadow.Title: Character Creator — Describe your Shadow
Shadow.Required: Describe the character's Shadow before continuing.
Shadow.BookLabel: The essence that follows all things
Shadow.Heading: What is the Shadow?
Shadow.Introduction: Every creature and object has a Shadow: the invisible expression of its essence and spiritual affinities. It may appear as a color, glow, mist, texture, or sensation without resembling a physical silhouette.
Shadow.Visibility: Witchsight and Holy Smoke make it possible to perceive it and interpret what it reveals. Its appearance describes who the character is within, but grants no bonus.
Shadow.IndexHint: Open a page to learn about each source and find inspiration for your Shadow.

Nature.Title: Nature
Nature.Text: Greens, reds, and whites; sap, leaves, blood, snow, mist, and organic forms.

Civilization.Title: Civilization
Civilization.Text: Gold, silver, and copper; polished metal, coins, precise lines, heraldry, and disciplined light.

Darkness.Title: Darkness
Darkness.Text: Abyssal black and signs of taint. Corruption often stains, corrodes, erases, or distorts other colors.

PageText.Nature: Shadows tied to Nature resemble living and untamed things: leaves stirred by an unseen wind, the red of blood, the white of snow, roots, bark, moss, and running water. They may be peaceful or fierce, but rarely appear perfectly ordered.
PageText.Civilization: Shadows tied to Civilization take the appearance of metals, coins, heraldry, precise lines, or crafted light. Gold, silver, and copper may express status, ambition, discipline, trade, or the influence of Ambrian institutions.
PageText.Darkness: Darkness reveals itself as absence, stain, and distortion. A corrupted Shadow may retain its original color while showing rust, cracks, ash, pale patches, or places that seem consumed by a silent void.

IllustrationAlt.Nature: A figure surrounded by a green Shadow of leaves, moss, and red veins.
IllustrationAlt.Civilization: A figure surrounded by a Shadow of gold, silver, copper, and ordered lines.
IllustrationAlt.Darkness: A figure surrounded by a dark violet Shadow marked by Corruption.

Shadow.MixedNote: A person may embody more than one principle. Mixed Shadows are common along the borders between Ambria and Davokar.
Shadow.CorruptionText: Corruption distorts the Shadow: gold is battered, silver darkens, copper corrodes, and natural colors gain pale stains, rust, or ash. If you wish, include a subtle sign that may grow during the story.
Shadow.ExamplesHint: Click an example to use it as a starting point, then change it freely.

Examples.Nature: Deep green like wet moss, crossed by red veins that pulse like sap.
Examples.Civilization: Silver like a well-kept blade, with orderly reflections moving around the body.
Examples.Mixed: Ancient copper at the edges, dissolving into green leaves stirred by an unseen wind.
Examples.Spiritual: White and gentle like mist resting over the lakes of Davokar at dawn.
Examples.Corrupted: Golden like a royal coin, but marked by small dark stains that seem to grow slowly.

Shadow.Placeholder: E.g. Silver like a blade under moonlight, with small rust stains close to the heart...
Shadow.FieldHint: Use one or two memorable sentences.

Equipment.Title: Character Creator — Choose Equipment
Equipment.AbilityEquipmentHint: Equipment granted by Abilities appears marked and will be added automatically. If no Ability grants a weapon, choose a starting combination.
Equipment.ShopSubtitle: Choose starting equipment and purchase items for the character
Equipment.ShowRules: Show or hide the starting equipment rules
Equipment.AbilityGrantReason: The {ability} Ability grants this item for free during character creation.
Equipment.BasicGrantReason: This item is part of the character's free starting equipment choice.
Equipment.LightArmorGrantReason: Every character who does not receive other armor from an Ability starts with Light Armor for free.
Equipment.CampingGrantReason: All characters start with Camping Equipment for free.
Equipment.MoneyFormula: {experience} total XP grants {thaler} thalers — 1 thaler for every 10 XP.
Equipment.PrivilegedStartingMoney: The Privileged trait replaces the normal calculation: the character starts with exactly {total} thalers.
Equipment.PariahStartingMoney: The Pariah trait replaces the normal calculation: the character starts with only {total} shillings.
Equipment.CampingAutomation: The original item is preserved. When opened on the sheet, Ind Resources can create and organize its contents without duplicates.
Equipment.MissingCamping: No accessible Camping Equipment world item was found.
Equipment.Required: Choose one of the starting weapon combinations.
Equipment.ChoiceStageText: Resolve the choices granted by Abilities or the starting combination first. You can then review free items and purchase additional equipment.
Equipment.NoMatchingItems: No compatible accessible world item was found.
Equipment.StartingChoiceHint: Choose one combination. The names describe the weapons narratively; the sheet receives the generic items for the indicated categories.
Equipment.NoAbilityGrants: None of the chosen Abilities grants a specific item from the Starting Equipment table.
Equipment.StartingRulesWeapons: The character receives the equipment connected to their Abilities for free. If no Ability grants a weapon, choose one of the combinations below.
Equipment.StartingRulesArmor: In addition to weapons, a character starts with light armor. If a player wants heavier armor, it must be purchased with starting money. It is wise to buy armor with the Flexible quality when affordable; Mystics may buy a witch gown, wizard cloak, or priest robe for that reason.
Equipment.OfficialIntroductionBeforeCamp: A character's starting equipment, weapons, and money are determined by their archetype or by the Abilities and powers selected by the player. All characters begin with
Equipment.OfficialIntroductionAfterCamp: . Trinkets suited to the character's background may be added at no cost: a deck of cards, pipe and tobacco, fishing rod and bait, a horn, or similar items are welcome as long as they make the character vivid. Keepsakes such as a lock of a loved one's hair, a wooden figurine of a deceased relative, or an embroidered handkerchief that is the only clue to the character's father's murderer truly enrich the character's story.
Equipment.AbilityGrantLead: Because you have the Abilities {abilities}, you receive the following items:
Equipment.NoAbilityGrantLead: None of your Abilities grants equipment, so you may begin with:
Equipment.ArmorIntroductionAfter: . If a player wants heavier armor, it must be purchased with starting money. It is wise to buy armor with the Flexible quality when affordable; Mystics may buy a witch gown, wizard cloak, or priest robe for that reason.
Equipment.ArmorAlreadyGranted: The Ability {ability} already grants armor to the character, so they do not also receive Light Armor.
Equipment.MarksmanChoice: Marksman lets you choose one of the weapons below:
Equipment.MarksmanRequired: Choose either a Crossbow or a Bow for the Marksman benefit.
Equipment.AbilityChoiceLead: The {ability} Ability lets you choose one of the following items:
Equipment.AbilityChoiceRequired: Choose the starting equipment granted by the {ability} Ability.
Equipment.AbilityChoiceHint: Select the equipment granted by the Ability before continuing.
Equipment.MarksmanAlsoReceives: Regardless of the choice, you also receive
Equipment.StaffCombination: A Sturdy Staff (Long Weapon) and a Dagger (Short Weapon)
Equipment.OneHandedCombination: A Sword (One-handed Weapon) and a Dagger (Short Weapon)
Equipment.RangedCombination: A Bow (Ranged Weapon), a Quiver, 10 Arrows, and a Dagger (Short Weapon)

Grants.ShortWeapon: A short weapon (such as a dagger)

Personality.Title: Character Creator — Background, Personality, and Shadow
Personality.Required: Fill in the name, appearance and personality, background, personal goal, and Shadow before continuing.
Personality.Introduction: Memorable details turn Attributes and Abilities into someone who belongs in the world of Symbaroum. It need not be long: a few clear sentences already give the Game Master material for encounters and adventures.

Questions.Origin: Where was the character born, and what brought them to the Davokar frontier?
Questions.Relationships: Who helped, harmed, or still expects something from them?
Questions.Temperament: How do they speak, react to danger, and treat strangers?
Questions.Motivation: What debt, dream, fear, or ambition keeps them moving?

Personality.QuoteHint: Choose a short quote that captures the character's manner of speaking and outlook on life.
Personality.GoalHint: The goal should create stories: something the Game Master can turn into choices, encounters, or adventures.
Personality.Name: Name
Personality.NamePlaceholder: What is the character known as?
Personality.QuotePlaceholder: A phrase they might say during play...
Personality.AppearancePlaceholder: Describe physical traits, clothing, gestures, temperament, and manner of speaking...
Personality.AppearanceHint: Saved to the official sheet's Appearance field.
Personality.BackgroundPlaceholder: Briefly tell where they came from, who shaped their life, and how they reached the start of the campaign...
Personality.BackgroundHint: Include people, places, or events that may return to the story.
Personality.GoalPlaceholder: What does the character wish to achieve, discover, protect, or overcome?
Personality.PersonalGoalHint: Prefer a concrete goal that can guide decisions during the campaign.

Friends.Title: Character Creator — Friends and Group
Friends.Required: This step is optional and may be completed without filling any fields.
Friends.CompanionsText: Use the sheet rows to record the other player characters. Rows may be left empty and completed later when the whole group is assembled.
Friends.GroupText: If the group has a name, record it. It may be a company, order, entourage, fellowship, expedition, or any name that helps unite the characters.
Friends.GoalText: In addition to personal goals, the characters should share something they wish to achieve. Major goals may last for the whole campaign; smaller goals may change as the story progresses.

Examples.Base: Establish a base for the group.
Examples.Threat: Remove a serious and known threat.
Examples.Alliance: Form an alliance with another faction.
Examples.Legend: Find a legendary location or artifact.

Friends.ExampleHint: A good collective goal creates decisions and conflicts; money, Experience, or better equipment are usually consequences rather than the main goal.
Friends.Name: Name
Friends.GroupGoalPlaceholder: What does everyone wish to achieve, protect, discover, or prevent?
Friends.GroupGoalHint: Optional field. You may define the group later during the campaign.

berserker.Name: Berserker
berserker.Quote: Keep your distance! I would not want to hurt you.
berserker.Summary: Spirits of rage follow you and fill you with uncontrolled ferocity in battle. Outside combat, your patient and thoughtful disposition makes the contrast both admired and feared.
berserker.Abilities: Berserker, Two-handed Force, Iron Fist, Recovery

duelist.Name: Duelist
duelist.Quote: Please avoid bleeding on me when I run you through.
duelist.Summary: Honor and glory mean everything to a warrior, especially when a name can be defended with style. You live by a code, and the fact that you remain alive speaks highly of your talent.

captain.Name: Captain
captain.Quote: Everything will be fine — just follow my commands!
captain.Summary: You are a born leader who built a military career on that gift. Swordplay keeps you alive, but your real strength lies in bringing out the best in allies, guiding them, and keeping them safe.

sellsword.Name: Sellsword
sellsword.Quote: My sword and my life, in exchange for your gold.
sellsword.Summary: Fighting has been your way of life — for money. After serving many masters, you learned that skill and the instinct to recognize which battles can be won are the keys to survival.
sellsword.Abilities: Shield Fighter, Man-at-arms, Polearm Mastery, Iron Fist

knight.Name: Knight
knight.Quote: You may take my life, but not my honor.
knight.Summary: You fight to break enemy lines and keep your own firm. Heavily protected on the outside and driven by duty within, you battle for your lord, your allies, and your own glory.
knight.Abilities: Two-handed Force, Bodyguard, Man-at-arms, Iron Fist

witch.Name: Witch
witch.Quote: Your will is inferior to Nature's. Accept it! Or die.
witch.Summary: The wilds are your home and your calling is to balance your needs with nature's. You bargain with spirits, understand the flows of the land, and draw power from the cycle of life and death.
witch.Abilities: Witchcraft, Natural Warrior, Mystical Power, Ritualist

sorcerer.Name: Sorcerer
sorcerer.Quote: There is another way, an easier way…
sorcerer.Summary: Driven by desperation or hunger for power, you follow the path of sorcery. Corruption closes in quickly, as do witchhunters, forcing you to choose between seeking greater power or pursuing redemption.

theurg.Name: Theurg
theurg.Summary: You are a priest gifted with mystical powers and unwavering faith in the Lawgiver. From that foundation flows extraordinary power to protect life and confront darkness.

wizard.Name: Wizard
wizard.Quote: Remarkable, this must be taken back for further study!
wizard.Summary: You were instructed in the secrets of the Ordo Magica. To you, mystical powers are extensions of the world's fundamental laws, carefully studied and applied to grand effect.

selfTaughtMystic.Name: Self-taught Mystic
selfTaughtMystic.Quote: They said I did not take my powers seriously; I will show them how wrong they are.
selfTaughtMystic.Summary: You learned alone, were excluded from the traditions, or rejected their narrow views. Freedom has a price: Corruption is always near and witchhunters and Black Cloaks consider you fair game.

charlatan.Name: Charlatan
charlatan.Quote: Two drops a day and you will never be sick again!
charlatan.Summary: You chose the social arena as your battlefield. A quick tongue is your sharpest weapon and trustworthy eyes your finest shield; if both fail, light weapons and stealthy movement remain.

witchhunter.Name: Witchhunter
witchhunter.Quote: I would rather put down an innocent than let a blight beast walk over them.
witchhunter.Summary: You devoted your life to fighting blight beasts. You wield steel, fire, and perhaps rituals taken from defeated foes, accepting even the risk of Corruption to battle evil with fanatical fervor.

thug.Name: Thug
thug.Quote: Your money or your blood — the choice is yours!
thug.Summary: You grew up where gangs teach how to profit from others' work beneath the watch's nose. You may act alone or serve nobles as an enforcer protected by your master's influence.

treasureHunter.Name: Treasure-hunter
treasureHunter.Quote: This altar… I wonder if it can be pushed aside…
treasureHunter.Summary: The depths of Davokar hide the treasures that sustain you. You dream of ruins and sunken temples and have developed a broad set of skills to survive the forest's dangers.

ranger.Name: Ranger
ranger.Quote: Anything alive can be tracked. And brought down…
ranger.Summary: Deep forests and mountain valleys are your home, where you hunt for food, hides, or the safety of travelers. You know how to stay beyond an enemy's reach while your arrows find their mark.
ranger.Abilities: Acrobatics, Marksman, Beast Lore, Sixth Sense

monsterHunter.Name: Monster Hunter
monsterHunter.Quote: Let me deal with your… problem.
monsterHunter.Summary: You have developed techniques for tracking and slaying creatures that threaten frontier settlements. Hunter societies compete and cooperate to keep settlements safe, study monsters, and trade valuable trophies.
monsterHunter.Abilities: Trapper, Marksman or Polearm Mastery, Beast Lore
monsterHunter.Gifts: Hunting Dog, Cartographer, Contacts, Bushcraft, Privileged, Servant, Porter

bountyHunter.Name: Bounty Hunter
bountyHunter.Quote: Scum, me? Sure, but scum is what you need, it seems.
bountyHunter.Summary: You hunt criminals, deserters, cultists, and other wanted targets. The most desperate fugitives seek refuge in Davokar, forcing bounty hunters to combine accuracy, vigilance, and capture techniques.
bountyHunter.Gifts: Hunting Dog, Contacts, Gossip, Enduring March, Bushcraft, Porter

runeSmith.Name: Rune Smith
runeSmith.Quote: The rhythm of the world echoes in the beat of my hammer.
runeSmith.Summary: You unite the craft of the forge with the discipline of combat, bearing arms and armor made by your own hands. The tradition is strongest among trolls but also attracts abductees, ogres, and other warrior-artisans.
runeSmith.Abilities: Blacksmith, Two-handed Force or Hammer Step, Iron Fist
runeSmith.Gifts: Forbidden Knowledge, Contacts, Heirloom, Enduring March, Porter

tattooedWarrior.Name: Tattooed Warrior
tattooedWarrior.Quote: My rage burns in my body; come closer, feel the heat!
tattooedWarrior.Summary: Symbols of power cover your body and turn fury into battlefield strength. Among the Vajvod these warriors serve their leaders; among goblins and trolls they form a feared elite.
tattooedWarrior.Abilities: Two-handed Force or Polearm Mastery, Iron Fist, Rune Tattoo

weaponMaster.Name: Weapon Master
weaponMaster.Quote: You want to live; I want to die and be remembered with admiration.
weaponMaster.Summary: You devote yourself to mastering one weapon and its philosophy of combat. You may follow the path of the Axe Artist, Spear Dancer, Sacred Sword, or Flail Fighter.
weaponMaster.Races: Barbarian, goblin, elf, abducted human, Ambrian, changeling, ogre, or troll
weaponMaster.Abilities: Axe Artist: Acrobatics, Axe Artist, Twin Attack; Spear Dancer: Acrobatics, Staff Fighting, Entangling or Polearm Mastery; Sacred Sword: Acrobatics, Blessed Sword, Man-at-arms; Flail Fighter: Entangling, Two-handed Force, Flail Fighter
weaponMaster.Gifts: Gambler, Contacts, Heirloom, Privileged, Robust, Servant, Commanding Voice

formerCultist.Name: Former Cultist
formerCultist.Quote: My Master's word was law; now survival is everything.
formerCultist.Summary: You abandoned a dark cult but carry memories, guilt, and enemies. Survival requires knowledge of poison, corruption, and the methods of those who now pursue you.
formerCultist.Gifts: Contacts, Doubletongue, Hideouts, False Identity, Mirage, Con Artist

guildThief.Name: Guild Thief
guildThief.Quote: What are you doing on my turf?
guildThief.Summary: You belong to the criminal tradition of Ambrian cities. Cunning, agility, discretion, and knowing who is untouchable separate a true guild member from a common thief.
guildThief.Abilities: Trapper, Knife Dance or Low Blow, Opportunist
guildThief.Gifts: Contacts, Dexterous, Hideouts, Burglar, Trickster, Con Artist

sapper.Name: Sapper
sapper.Quote: Your armor and walls are my combustion chamber.
sapper.Summary: Trained in sieges, fortifications, and alchemical weapons, you bring down walls and enemy positions. Some sappers serve armies; others take their dangerous knowledge on expeditions into Davokar.
sapper.Abilities: Alchemy or Blacksmith, Two-handed Force or Man-at-arms, Siege Expert
sapper.Gifts: Forbidden Knowledge, Dexterous, Contacts, Enduring March, Porter

trollSinger.Name: Troll Singer
trollSinger.Quote: My voice echoes with the harmony of creation.
trollSinger.Summary: Your voice reveals mysteries, inspires allies, and wins battles. This skaldic tradition is strongest among trolls, elves, and dwarves, often uniting poetry, leadership, and physical might.
trollSinger.Abilities: Troll Singing, Leader, Mystical Power (usually Combat Hymn)
trollSinger.Gifts: Archivist, Contacts, Heirloom, Musician, Storyteller, Commanding Voice

symbolist.Name: Symbolist
symbolist.Quote: I draw, and the world obeys.
symbolist.Summary: You build power through runes, signs, and symbols. The tradition came from the east and is especially influential among Clan Vajvod, where its practitioners rival witches in authority.
symbolist.Races: Barbarian of Clan Vajvod, goblin, or troll
symbolist.Abilities: Mystical Power (usually Protective Runes), Ritualist (usually Carve Rune Tattoo), Symbolism

Storage.InventoryEmpty: No loose items in the inventory.

ExplorerLicense.Introduction: Introduced in the autumn of Year 15, the Explorer's License regulates travel and exploration in Davokar Forest. It may cover one person, a group, or an entire organization, by month or by year.
ExplorerLicense.RequiredText: An Ambrian expedition wishing to enter Davokar legally must present a license matching both the party and its stated purpose.
ExplorerLicense.IssuerYndaros: At the City Watch headquarters in Yndaros.
ExplorerLicense.IssuerThistleHold: At the Queen's Legation in Thistle Hold.
ExplorerLicense.GroupRule: A company needs a suitable collective license; combining individual licenses does not replace the party's document.
ExplorerLicense.HowItWorks: How it works at the table
ExplorerLicense.StepRegister: Declare the number of participants and choose monthly or yearly validity.
ExplorerLicense.StepAssess: State the expedition's objectives, gathered resources, wagons, and other circumstances; the licensor calculates the add-ons.
ExplorerLicense.StepCarry: Carry the document during the journey and present it to the Queen's Rangers when requested.
ExplorerLicense.BaseCostHint: The base amount covers the listed party size. The shop list price represents only an individual license; groups should use this table.
ExplorerLicense.AdditionsHint: Gathering, harvesting, and exploration are part of the basic assessment. Inexperience, intentions, and other charges depend on the licensor's judgment.
ExplorerLicense.WithoutLicenseText: Being caught in Davokar without suitable documents may result in severe fines and physical punishment. A patrol may also challenge discrepancies between the license and the actual expedition.
